back2basics.text: A GLOF occurs when a glacial lake, formed by melting glaciers, suddenly releases large volumes of water due to dam failure or breach. These floods can cause rapid downstream flooding, threatening lives and infrastructure. GLOFs are increasingly frequent due to climate change accelerating glacier melt, especially in mountainous regions like the Himalayas.

2026-10-30-pm-3cf828aabe.deck: A glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) from Bhutan's Sintaphu lake caused a flood alert in northern West Bengal and Assam, prompting evacuation of over 4,000 people. This event highlights the risks of Himalayan glacial lakes and the importance of disaster preparedness and climate change adaptation in the region.

back2basics.text: Government securities are debt instruments issued by the government to borrow money from the public and financial institutions. Underwriting auctions involve Primary Dealers committing to buy a minimum amount of securities, ensuring the government can raise the required funds. The underwriting commission is the fee paid to these dealers for their commitment and risk.

2026-10-30-pm-4c25c5ba39.deck: The Reserve Bank of India conducted an underwriting auction for government securities worth ₹33,000 crore on October 30, 2026. body.label: Auction details
body.text: The Government of India announced the sale of government securities worth ₹33,000 crore through an underwriting auction held on October 30, 2026.

body.label: Securities and amounts
body.text: The securities included 6.20% GS 2029 (₹9,000 crore), 6.57% GS 2033 (₹12,000 crore), 7.63% GS 2056 (₹9,000 crore), and 7.50% GOI SGrB 2056 (₹3,000 crore).

body.label: Role of Primary Dealers
body.text: Primary Dealers (PDs) had minimum underwriting commitments and bidding commitments under Additional Competitive Underwriting (ACU) for each security, ensuring market support for the auction.

body.label: Auction method and timing
body.text: The auction was conducted through a multiple price-based method, with PDs submitting bids electronically between 09:00 A.M. and 09:30 A.M. on the auction day.

sections.heading: What was the underwriting auction conducted on October 30, 2026?

body.label: Total underwriting achieved
body.text: The total amount underwritten matched the notified amount of ₹33,000 crore, with each security fully underwritten by PDs.

body.label: Underwriting commission rates
body.text: The RBI set the cut-off underwriting commission rates per ₹100 at 0.92 paise for 6.20% GS 2029, 0.64 paise for 6.57% GS 2033, 0.74 paise for 7.63% GS 2056, and 1.00 paise for 7.50% GOI SGrB 2056.

body.label: Fiscal and market impact
body.text: This auction supports government borrowing requirements and maintains liquidity and stability in government securities markets.

back2basics.concept: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) in Welfare Schemes
back2basics.text: Direct Benefit Transfer is a mechanism where government subsidies or financial assistance are transferred directly into the bank accounts of beneficiaries. This reduces leakages, ensures timely payments, and increases transparency and efficiency in welfare delivery. PM-KISAN uses DBT to provide income support directly to farmers, helping them meet agricultural and household needs without intermediaries.

2026-10-30-pm-58cd8810d6.deck: On October 30, 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi released the 24th instalment of the PM-KISAN scheme, transferring more than ₹18,690 crore directly to over 9.34 crore farmers. This event highlights the government's ongoing commitment to farmer welfare and rural economic empowerment through direct income support and agricultural infrastructure development.

back2basics.text: The judiciary interprets laws passed by the legislature but also relies on the Constitution when statutes are silent or ambiguous. The Constitution is the supreme law that guarantees fundamental rights and principles such as dignity, liberty, and equality. Courts balance respect for legislative intent with protecting constitutional values, especially in new or unforeseen situations.

2026-10-30-pm-64b432f39d.deck: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant emphasized that when statutes do not provide answers, the judiciary must rely on the Constitution’s promises of dignity, liberty, and equality. This principle is crucial for UPSC aspirants to understand the judiciary’s role in constitutional interpretation and adapting law to new challenges like technology.

back2basics.text: Disaster management involves preparedness, response, relief, and rehabilitation activities coordinated by central and state governments. It includes early warning systems, evacuation, rescue operations, and restoration of essential services to reduce the impact of natural calamities like cyclones and floods.

body.label: Fatalities and damage
body.text: Cyclone Arnab caused five deaths in Andhra Pradesh due to falling trees, electric poles, electrocution, and collapsing walls; Odisha experienced heavy rainfall affecting 17 districts with no major deaths reported yet.

body.label: Crop and infrastructure loss
body.text: Over 70,000 hectares of agricultural crops and more than 10,500 hectares of horticultural crops were damaged in Andhra Pradesh; power supply was disrupted for over 25 lakh non-farm and nearly one lakh farm connections, with thousands of electric poles and transformers damaged.

body.label: Displacement and evacuations
body.text: More than 30,000 people were evacuated in Odisha from low-lying and landslide-prone areas; relief camps were set up in Andhra Pradesh with provisions of food and financial aid to affected families.

body.label: Central government assistance
body.text: Union Home Minister Amit Shah assured full assistance to affected states and directed National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams to conduct rescue and relief operations on a war footing.

body.label: State government measures
body.text: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu sought central aid, announced compensation of ₹5 lakh to families of the deceased, and financial support to affected farmers and households; Telangana extended support for restoration works.

body.label: Impact assessment and monitoring
body.text: Impact Monitoring and Coordination Teams (IMCTs) were to be deployed to assess damage and determine further assistance; meteorological departments monitored cyclone weakening and forecasted rainfall and flood risks.

back2basics.concept: Judicial Intervention in Religious Institution Management
back2basics.text: Religious institutions in India are often managed by hereditary or community groups, but courts can intervene when maladministration harms heritage or public interest. Judicial oversight ensures accountability, proper maintenance, and protection of cultural assets while respecting religious customs.

back2basics.text: Electoral rolls are official lists of eligible voters in a constituency. They are periodically updated to add new voters and remove names of those who have died, moved away, or are otherwise ineligible. The Election Commission of India conducts revisions like the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) to maintain accurate voter lists, which is essential for free and fair elections.

body.label: Mass deletions
body.text: The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) reduced Belagavi’s voter count from 41,53,775 in January 2025 to 34,94,913, excluding 6,58,862 voters or 15.8% of the electorate.

body.label: Higher than state average
body.text: Belagavi’s deletion percentage is higher than Karnataka’s average of around 12%, though lower than Bengaluru’s 43% deletion rate.

body.label: Constituency-wise impact
body.text: All 18 Assembly seats in Belagavi saw an average deletion of 36,603 votes each, with some constituencies like Belgaum Dakshin and Yamkanamardi experiencing tens of thousands of deletions.

body.text: Among the deleted voters, approximately 1,03,839 were Muslims, with significant numbers in constituencies like Belgaum Uttar and Kudachi.

body.text: Complaints surfaced about misuse of Form 7 applications, including document fudging and intimidation, with political leaders from BJP and Congress accusing each other of violating rules.

body.text: Voters are categorized as Absent, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate, and Others (ASDDO) for deletion during the SIR.

body.text: Third-party objections to voter names are filed using Form 7, which has been a source of controversy due to alleged misuse.

back2basics.text: The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) is a constitutional authority responsible for conducting free and fair elections in India. The CEC enjoys security of tenure and can only be removed by a process similar to that of a Supreme Court judge, which involves a parliamentary impeachment for proven misbehavior or incapacity. This process ensures the independence of the Election Commission from executive interference.
